correctness.rationale: Every cyclic order-five binary de Bruijn word determines a unique bijective shift-register Boolean map on 16 four-bit tails, and vice versa when its 00000 orbit has full 32-period. All 65536 maps are exhausted; exactly 2048 pass. Independently, all Euler circuits of the binary four-gram graph rooted at edge 00000 yield exactly the same 2048 canonical words. Two independent discrepancy computations agree pointwise and give 224,688,912,224. The actual bundled verifier reproduced these results. No finite experiment is extrapolated to higher order.

originality.rationale: The exact full order-five population discrepancy histogram is not implied by the known lex-least cycle analysis, a study of selected construction families, or the general minimum-discrepancy theorem. Full texts/material passages were compared on claims and ranges, not title overlap. Exact web searches and available research-claim comparisons did not expose equivalent or dominating full-population multiplicity data. Historical unindexed tables remain an expressly recorded risk.

value.rationale: Circular local-balance discrepancy is a mathematically motivated invariant of de Bruijn pseudorandom cycles, and Gabric–Sawada specifically identify the population discrepancy distribution as a research direction. The first 2048-member binary instance has a genuinely complete distribution: prevalence of minimum and maximum discrepancy, exact mean, and confirmation of a proposed extremum in this order. This is more informative than construction-only examples and does not depend on an unproved generalization.
